title: dwf-motr-master-of-the-ring
label: Chris Courtade

won.source: The federation's own FAQ and application of 22 August 2001: at the Master of the Ring III pay-per-view, DWF World Champion Chris Courtade beat Rick Styles, Bad Eye McBaine and William Craven to end up the Ultimate Master.

note: The third edition's winner, as the federation later recounted it; the July 2000 final card itself survives as a preview.

title: dwf-motr-master-of-the-ring
label: "Cool Hand" Luke Kinsey

won.source: A sixth Master of the Ring title match, ordered on the spot by promoter Nick Demola and contested as the seventh tournament broadcast's own opening bout; Kinsey won by pinfall with a Gannosuke Clutch.

note: Billed into this match as the already-recognized sixth champion; the bout settled a year-old dispute over the sixth tournament's own result rather than crowning a first-time winner.

won.source: War of Attrition -- Master of the Ring III (13-15 July 2000): billed as the second SuperBout, a Ladder Match against James Pillow, both introduced as former INWI champions; the promotion's own later retrospective ("Oh yeah, we're back") confirms Van Strife defeated Pillow.
The third Pentagon Pain match, a six-man bout against Eugene Robinson, Justin Cage, Rick Marley, Ryan Delaney, and David Rheaume; November won by pinfall.

War of Attrition -- Master of the Ring III (13-15 July 2000): billed as the third SuperBout, a "Demola Rules Match" against Alex Martinez with promotion president Nick Demola as guest referee; the promotion's own later retrospective ("Oh yeah, we're back") confirms Keening defeated Martinez.
SuperBout VII, a brawl against Eddie Jacobs that opened with both men crashing a van through the arena entrance; McBaine won by pinfall, becoming a two-time SuperBout champion.

title: dwf-motr-atlantic-storm
label: "Cream of the Crop" Mike Waldrop

won.source: Not stated: the federation's own update of 27 August 2001 lists him as the reigning Atlantic Storm Champion when it reopened, with every other title vacant.

note: Listed as champion in the current rankings of the 27 August 2001 update; how and when he won the title is not recorded.
